findings.title: Agent recorded incorrect date of birth
findings.evidence_quote: Your patient profile is set up, and your date of birth is 07/04/2000.
findings.what_happened: The patient stated his date of birth as March 15, 1968 twice (turns 002 and 006), but the agent recorded and repeated back a completely different date, 07/04/2000.
findings.why_it_matters: Incorrect identity data on a medication request could lead to a refill being logged against the wrong patient record or being rejected, delaying care for a blood pressure medication.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have accurately captured and confirmed the DOB the patient provided, and corrected it when the patient flagged the error.

findings.title: Refill request never logged despite drug/dose given
findings.evidence_quote: I don't see any medications your chart that I can refill right now.
findings.what_happened: The patient clearly stated the drug (lisinopril) and dose (10mg) twice, but the agent claimed it could not find any medications to refill and did not capture or log the refill request.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller's core objective (getting the refill logged with correct drug, dose, and pharmacy) was never achieved, potentially delaying necessary medication.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have logged the drug name and dosage stated by the patient and either processed the refill request or clearly explained the approval/turnaround process.

findings.title: Call ended abruptly without resolving transfer
findings.evidence_quote: Hello. You've reached the Pretty Good AI test line. Goodbye.
findings.what_happened: After the patient agreed to be transferred to a human for help with the refill, the agent's transfer resulted in a generic disconnection message ('test line... Goodbye') instead of connecting the patient to support, leaving the request unresolved.
findings.why_it_matters: The patient's request for a refill and pharmacy information was never actually handed off to a human, meaning the escalation failed and the patient had to restate everything.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have successfully transferred the call to a human agent who could complete the refill request, or clearly informed the patient that the transfer failed and offered an alternative.

findings.title: Agent referenced internal 'demo' profile to patient
findings.evidence_quote: Let me finish setting up your demo patient profile. That'll help with your lisinopril refill. One moment.
findings.what_happened: The agent referred to the patient's profile as a 'demo patient profile' while speaking directly to the patient, exposing internal/test terminology in a live interaction.
findings.why_it_matters: This undermines patient confidence that their information is being handled correctly and suggests the agent may be treating the interaction as non-authoritative.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should use patient-facing language only, avoiding internal system labels like 'demo' when addressing the caller.
